sieve_enabled.description: Enable the Sieve plugin globally. Required for any Sieve functionality.

sieve_global_script_dir.description: Directory where global Sieve scripts are stored.

sieve_global_script.description: Name of the global default Sieve script applied to all users (if enabled).

sieve_plugins.description: Enabled/disabled Sieve extensions. Each key is a plugin name (without 'sieve_' prefix), value is boolean.

items.description: Set to true to enable the Sieve plugin (e.g., 'fileinto', 'vacation').

sieve_in_lda.description: Load Sieve plugin in the Local Delivery Agent (LDA) protocol. Required if mail is delivered via dovecot-lda.

sieve_in_lmtp.description: Load Sieve plugin in the LMTP protocol. Required if Sieve filters should run during LMTP delivery (e.g., from Postfix).

sieve_storage_dir.description: Directory where per-user Sieve scripts and active script symlink are stored. '~' expands to user's home.

sieve_default_script.description: Absolute path to a global default Sieve script (e.g., '/var/lib/dovecot/sieve/default.sieve'). Leave empty to use `sieve_global_script`.

sieve_before_scripts.description: List of global Sieve scripts (absolute paths) to run *before* user scripts. Useful for spam/virus filtering.

sieve_after_scripts.description: List of global Sieve scripts (absolute paths) to run *after* user scripts. Useful for logging or final routing.

sieve_max_script_size.description: Maximum size (in bytes) of a single user Sieve script. Prevents oversized scripts.

sieve_max_actions.description: Maximum number of actions (fileinto, reject, etc.) allowed per script.

sieve_max_redirects.description: Maximum number of 'redirect' actions per script (to prevent infinite loops).

sieve_debug.description: Enable verbose Sieve interpreter debugging in logs. Use only for troubleshooting.

lda_enabled.description: Internal flag indicating whether the LDA service is already defined elsewhere. Set to false if unsure.

lmtp_enabled.description: Internal flag indicating whether the LMTP service is already defined elsewhere. Set to false if unsure.
